messages.text: Did Roberto ever answer about Sunday? I can remind him if you want.
You free after your soup is put away?
He sent one line back. Said the drive from San Antonio is too much this month.
Yes. Ring me at 7:45. Ten minutes is fine; I only need the real update, not the whole neighborhood report.
That's about what I expected. Did he say if both boys are coming for Easter?
Good. I wrote down the lab number and the water bill question so I don't forget.
No, just that they are busy with their own places and jobs. I told him to keep me posted.
That is why I ask you. You bring the paper and the facts.
I found that slim book of word grids at the used shop. Want me to hold it until Wednesday?
Yes, please. I still have last Sunday's folded page on the arm of the chair, pencil marks everywhere.
Then no more tiny boxes after 10 tonight. Put on that moonlight piece and give your hands something calmer to do.
Blue yarn is already beside the teacup. I just need to stop peeking at 14 Across.
For Saturday's table, should I print the food-box signs with "frijoles" first and the other wording underneath?
Yes, that feels right for the older ladies. Mama always read that line first before anything from City Hall.
I also found the old recipe card from Tia Rosa. The measurements jump from cups to puñados like our aunties wrote them.
That is exactly how our kitchen sounded growing up. School papers one way, supper table another.
For Saturday, do you want me to set aside the long table by the hall kitchen or leave it for the elders' plates?
Leave that one for plates. I can bring the beans already cooled and the dough wrapped tight so we are not rushing.
Good. If you stop by El Rancho, can you check for the sour cream in the blue lid? The one from the regular store was too sweet last time.
I will go after work Friday. I need masa anyway, and they usually have the beans that hold up better.
The blue sedan is back by the corner store. Same one from yesterday?
Rain looks close. Still doing the short loop at 6:15?
Rain looks light. Still meeting by the Trinity trail sign at 6:20?
I saw it. Let's change to the school route and keep walking. No phone call unless someone is actually in trouble.
Short loop only. I want the extra 15 minutes before work to move the Toyota payment into the register.
Yes, shorter loop. I have to stop by Elena's after work to pick up that old college box.
Route by the school again? The crosswalk guard said they still have no working lights on that corner.
Yes, let's see it in daylight. I want to compare it with that bond list before I mark my ballot.
I wrote the plate down just in case.
Good. Bring the light jacket. I will wait by the benches.
The one with your lab notebooks and the letter you never mailed?
Good. Time, plate, and what we saw only. If Mrs. Alvarez asks later, we can help her make a clean report.
That's the one. Tasha wants the notes on safe holding temps, and Elena said the envelope is still tucked inside.
Leaving now. I am keeping the morning tidy so nothing gets squeezed.
You always bring your notes to the walk.
Notes help me ask better questions later. I am not made for standing downtown with signs, but I can still pay attention.
I finished the first schedule draft. Vendor sheets are in the manager folder too.
Thank you. My shoulders finally dropped after I wrote tomorrow's list and put the kettle on.
Good. I can handle the breakfast swap calls before you get in.
Please do. I am going to knit two rows and leave the phone across the room.
I found Mama's old white shoes in the hall closet, the ones with the rubber soles.
Keep them for now. She wore those long before she switched to the hairnet and tray line.
I also found Daddy's big ring of keys with the little brass tag from the boiler room.
Put that with the photos. The kids always ask why he carried so many.
Someone in study group passed me a loud screenshot about the new spring shots. No name on it, just red circles.
I would not pass that along. I am going to ask Dr. Morales on Friday and see what the clinic handout says.
Good. Bring it Wednesday if you want and we can compare it with something that has a date on it.
Yes, date and author first. The exclamation marks do not count.
For Saturday, I moved the volunteer table away from the patio side. Last time that corner made your eyes water.
Thank you. I will take the coffee station instead and bring the hibiscus tea.
Also, Rosa is bringing rum cake. I told her you usually just take a small slice and coffee.
That is plenty for me. I need a clear head for the food boxes and the older folks' cars.
Still hearing the wind on my side. Are you skipping the 6:15 loop?
Yes. I want daylight first, then I may walk only as far as Mrs. Coleman's fence.
Good. That corner always gets branches down after a loud night.
I'll take my small flashlight and the spare gloves before coffee.
Mrs. C, I can cover the last vendor call if you need to get home for your sister.
Thank you. Elena sounded tired, so I want the eggplant and zucchini already soft when she gets here.
You always send people home with something warm. I will finish the produce notes.
Use the basil and thyme list from my desk if the produce guy asks. I am saving the little chilled bottle for the table.
Before I forget, did you write down this morning's cuff numbers for Dr. Ramos?
Yes, 122 over 76 before breakfast. I took the little white one after coffee, same as always.
Good. And don't leave the bedtime one in your purse again after lunch tomorrow.
Already moved it to the nightstand. I am keeping the March card checked off.
Do you still have that blue League booklet? Mine disappeared under the stack of study papers.
I have it. I underlined the school board section and the two city council biographies.
Good. Bring it Wednesday if you can. I want to hear what you thought of the Place 4 answers.
I will. I also want to ask Deacon Luis whether he was at the parish forum last month.
Can you take the front table tomorrow? I have Rudy on the rice sacks, but nobody steady for the sign-in sheet.
Yes, I can be there by 8:15. I will bring tape and the black marker from my kitchen drawer.
Good. Also save two lighter bags for Dona Lidia and Mr. Flores. They both asked if you were coming.
Tell them I will walk theirs out myself if the lot is crowded.
The produce vendor changed the Friday delivery window again. Do you want me to call or wait for you?
You call. Use the note I put under tab 4 and ask for an email confirmation before noon.
Got it. I’ll write down who I speak with and add it to the sheet.
Good. I’ll look after lunch, but I’m not stepping in unless there’s a real snag.
I filled the first draft for the 9th-15th. Still short one lunch runner on Tuesday.
Good. Mark Tuesday in yellow and do not post until every food prep slot has a named person.
Payroll portal looks slow today. Mine finally showed the new statement.
I saw mine at lunch. Same pattern as usual: 5,600 up top, about 4,100 hitting checking after everything comes out.
Good. I was worried the system held back the deposits again.
Got it. I also put the thermometer check beside each opening cook.
That is the habit I want you to keep. A blank box turns into three calls before sunrise.
It landed, so I can finish the Sunday paper stack without guessing.
I sent you the draft for next week. I kept your floor walk at 8 and the office wrap-up at 5:15 like usual.
Thank you. I will review it after I close my Friday notes. Keep my dentist hour blocked on Thursday so I don't lose that slot.
Done. Do you want me to move the vendor call away from that morning?
Yes, put vendor follow-up after lunch. I can still leave by 5:30 if nothing catches fire.
Should I come by before lunch or after? I do not want to be in the way if the counters are covered.
After 1 is better. The first loaf will be cooling, and I can put the pepper starts back by the window.
Fine. I will bring the container you left here, and maybe you can send me home with a few basil leaves.
Yes. Floors were Thursday, so the kitchen should still be decent unless the flour wins.
Did the plumber ever call you back about that kitchen leak?
Yes, he can come Tuesday morning. He said it may be around $400 if the valve is the problem.
That is a lot, hermana. Do you need me to sit with you while he is there?
Come if you want coffee, but the money part is already set aside. I just need him to text before he arrives.
The Bishop Arts shop has a used Bruges guide in the window, the one with the canal map folded inside.
Please do not let me buy it yet unless it is under $8. I am still comparing that stack with the Portugal pages.
I can hold it at the counter while we have coffee. You said the blue envelope got only a small bit this month?
Yes. The house-and-medical cushion has to stay where I promised myself it would.
For the food table today, Mrs. Rivas asked if you still have that city handout about clinic signups and rental help.
I put three copies in my tote. I also marked the council office number that actually called me back last month.
Good. People trust the one that answers the phone more than the one with the loud mailers.
Exactly. If they cannot handle a pothole request or a benefits form, I do not need their speeches.
They moved the River City start to 6:30 on the page. Wind advisory near the bridge.
I saw it after checking the group notice. I'll meet you by the library side instead.
Clouds look heavy. Want to just do the short loop by Glendale Park?
Short loop is good. I need to be back before the plumber taps on the back door.
Good. If your knees complain, text me before you leave the house.
I will. I already called Elena last night about the ache, so this morning can just be a shorter loop.
No problem. If he comes early, holler and I can wait by the corner.
Thanks. I left the side gate unlocked, but there is nobody else there to hear him.
I moved Luis to Tuesday close and put Nina on prep Wednesday. Can you look before I post it?
Check Nina's hours first. We are already tight after the linen invoice, and I still need the produce order in by 3.
Got it. Also, the bride's aunt called again about the tray count for the 19th.
Tell her I will confirm after I see the final guest number. Use the same note format from the blue binder, the one I started here in 2012.
I found two white tablecloths in the parish closet. Do you want one for Mami's little table on the 18th?
Yes, thank you. I'll bring the framed picture and the small rosary from her nightstand.
Should I leave room for the candles and the soup sign-up sheet, like we did when people were bringing meals to your house?
Please. That old sign-up book still has the 2018 tabs, so I'll use a fresh page this time.
Are you staying through dinner service today, or should I cover the last vendor call?
I can stay, but I need ten minutes after prep to do the floor mat set in the office.
Got it. I put the shipment clipboard on your desk and left room by the chair.
Thank you. I also brought the black lace-ups today, so I should last better on the tile.
I marked the chapter on Reconstruction with a receipt so you can find my note.
Good. I finished the Lincoln one last night and put it in my tote for Wednesday.
Then Saturday coffee can be lighter talk. Same little place near Bishop Arts?
Yes, 10:00 if the parking is not too wild.
Linda says the south gate is still muddy. Want the community center side instead?
Yes, that side is better. I can do 6:15 to 6:45 before I need to get ready.
Still meeting at 6:15? It looks clear until 7.
Yes. I stayed up later with my Sunday envelopes, so I may be quiet for the first block.
Good. I'll park near the benches and text Linda.
Bring the small flashlight. That corner by the school is still dark.
I'll bring the small towel in case the path is still wet.
Already in my pocket. March is sitting at 3,420 after I added Kroger and the light bill, so at least that part is settled.
For Saturday, can you label the rice boxes in both columns again? The older ladies were reading your cards first last time.
Yes. I will write them tonight after dinner. No one should have to ask twice in front of the table.
Also, Dona Lidia wants the baleada list the way your mother used to say it.
I remember. Frijoles, queso, mantequilla. I promised her I would keep that wording.
After study, do you still want the little card with the quiet-office numbers from the parish table?
Yes, tuck it in your book. I keep thinking I should call, then the next staff problem eats the morning.
Are we still doing coffee after study, or did the restaurant pull you back in?
Coffee is still on. I made myself leave after Tasha brought me the draft and the cooler sheets matched.
I will bring it. Coffee first, then bookstore if the line is short.
Coffee sounds right. I baked lemon bars tonight so my hands would have something useful to do.
That sounds like progress for you.
I am trying. After that week in February, I need someone else to see the whole board before it lands on the wall.
I saved you a chair after study. Are you bringing the article with the school boundary maps?
Yes. I underlined the part about families crossing three bus routes for the same services another area has nearby.
Coffee after? We can talk through it before everyone starts giving speeches.
Coffee is better for me. I want to listen first, then decide what questions to bring to early voting.
For Saturday distribution, Mrs. Alvarado asked if that church flyer about the booster table is real.
Tell her I called the Dallas County number on the parish bulletin. They said the table is 10 to 1, and the nurse will bring the forms.
Perfect. I will toss the shiny handbill from the parking lot then. It had no phone number.
Yes. If they cannot put a person or office behind it, we do not use it at the tables.
Are you making the thick tortillas for lunch Sunday or should I bring bakery bread?
I put Mama and Papa's naturalization copies in the blue envelope. The consulate stamp is still clear.
I already bought the masa. Bring the cheese if you can, and I will make the beans early before Mass.
Good. I'll keep it with my Dallas certificate so we don't have three boxes open on Sunday.
I'll bring cheese and the little jar of curtido. Mama would laugh at us measuring everything now.
Do you remember Papa making us answer him at home before we ran off talking like schoolgirls?
I do. He would tap the table and wait until we said it right.
She measured with her hand and somehow it came out right. I still need a spoon.
Coffee after study is getting noisy over there. Want to skip it and trade books in the parking lot?
Yes, please. I have Elena at 7:45 and I don't want a long table of people tonight.
I'll bring the mystery paperback and keep it quick.
Perfect. You say quick and you mean quick.
After study, are you still stopping at Bishop Arts for coffee or going straight home?
Coffee is fine. I want to compare those judicial cards. I crossed off the one who only talked in cable-news lines.
Bring yours. I want to see who wrote about translator access and complaint records instead of just slogans.
That is what I circled too, plus the candidate who listed case backlogs and how to publish the numbers each month.
For the food boxes Saturday, should I save two extra Honduran coffee bags for Roberto's boys if they pass through?
Better not hold them. They almost never come this way unless Roberto gives them a reason.
Understood. I will keep the extras for the older parish ladies instead.
Thank you. If he texts from San Antonio before Friday, I can still ask.
Can you tap going on the Honduran flyer so more cousins see Saturday's food box time?
Done. I also shared Father Luis's table note and nothing else.
Thank you. And about Mrs. Rivas needing rides, better we call Lupe and Nestor tonight.
Yes, I'll call Lupe after supper. That part should stay between us.
For Saturday, should I put the milk crates near the side door or keep them by the tables?
Side door, but keep the cold bags last. I learned that lesson doing church suppers back in '94 when everybody wanted to open boxes too early.
I'll tape the list to the cooler lid. Do you want me to ask two teens to carry boxes for the older folks?
Yes, and have them write times on the sheet, not just names. It saves questions later.
Still meeting at 6:15? Heat looks quiet until later.
Yes. I’m keeping the phone zipped today. Tasha has the schedule draft and I promised myself not to hover.
Still walking? Radar looks clear until seven.
Yes, 6:15 is good. I need the steps before another 8-to-5:30 day.
Still walking at 6:15? It is already sticky outside.
Still good for 6:15, or did the little squares keep you up again?
Good. Bring water and your knee sleeve. We’ll do the river loop, not the long hill.
Storm line looks close. Are we shortening the walk?
Yes, but let's keep it to the shorter loop. My home cuff was fine, and I already took the breakfast pill.
I am coming. The last corner of the page would not behave, so I let Diamonds & Rust play twice and worked a few rows.
Yes, just the small loop. I have vegetables salted on towels and need to get them into the pot before work.
Short loop then. You said you had that eye place after work tomorrow, right?
That works. I want the morning to belong to my feet for once.
Tomorrow at 5:45. I just need to bring the little card from my wallet.
Short route then. Bring the blue jacket; wind is sharp.
That is early cooking. Somebody must be getting a nice plate.
Short loop works. Bring water; we can skip the hill by the school.
On my porch now. I packed the oat bar Janice gave me instead of stopping for biscuits.
Marisol is taking two containers to the parish freezer. I clipped parsley and basil before the rain started.
Vendor called back. Do you want me to confirm the standing order or wait for you?
Can I borrow the handout you mentioned for cooling rice and beans safely? The crew listens better when it comes from your old class binder.
Confirm it, please. Use the written steps in the binder and send me the final number.
I put it in your mailbox with the chart from my senior menu project.
Done. Also I started next week's schedule with two backup names for Friday night.
Thank you. Also, that sealed packet fell out of the folder. Want me to leave it alone?
Please. It belongs with the year I chose the house on Polk Street over another campus.
That helps. Leave the backups in place until we see the weather and reservations.
Do you still want me to close tomorrow? I can finish the vendor calls before lunch.
Yes, thank you. I am stopping by the management office on Lancaster after work to ask about the porch light.
Got it. Want me to text if the produce guy changes the delivery window?
Please do. If I miss it, I will see it when I get back to my place in 75216.
Are you resting tomorrow morning or going back to St. Matthew with Marisol?
Resting this Saturday. My next one is the 21st unless she calls short-handed.
Good. Last time you came home with your shoes muddy and your hands sore from all those cartons.
I know. But they needed extra hands for the car line.
For Saturday's table, should I bring extra gloves and the hair covers like your mama used to keep in her purse?
Yes, she would fuss if we handled bread bare-handed. She learned that after the place with all the little trays.
And I found two folding ladders. Your dad would have checked every hinge before letting us use them.
He checked hinges, pipes, lights, everything. Bring the sturdier one.
If you and Janice pass by Lucky Dog Books tomorrow, ask if they still have the Texas presidents shelf by the front.
We may stop after coffee. She is looking for a clean copy for me to borrow.
Good. Also tell her I saved two boxes from the hall for Wednesday.
For Saturday distribution, do you want the parking volunteers to call the city number if that man starts yelling again?
Have two volunteers stay with the older folks first. If he blocks the doors or touches anyone, then call.
And if someone comes out with a badge?
One person greets them, one writes names and times, and nobody gets talked down to while people are waiting for food.
Still walking at 6:15, or are you stopping by Laurel Land first?
Let's do the short loop. I want to place flowers for Papi before traffic gets bad.
Got it. Same gate by the 2011 stone?
Yes. I also need to be home after, Elena is picking up the old shower chair and the blood pressure cuff.
If you ever take those ten days you mentioned, I can handle vendor calls and the first schedule draft.
Maybe later in the year. I am only collecting prices for the old-city route right now.
Was that the Bruges one or the Portugal one?
Both are still in pencil. Nothing gets booked if the cushion dips below my line.
Payroll portal is showing the new benefit screen again. Did yours make you re-click anything?
It asked me to confirm the same 6% to Fidelity. I left it alone and printed the March paystub.
Good to know. I was afraid it erased mine.
Check before Monday. I also keep a separate tab for the house drafts so payroll surprises do not tangle with bills.
Vendor dinner got moved to Monday at 6. They picked that new place with the long bar and the patio heaters.
Reserve us an inside table if you can. I will order tea or one glass with dinner, then head home.
Got it. And I will handle the late close so you are not stuck there after the vendor pitch.
Good. I do not like mixing business decisions with anything that makes me foggy.
Are you still taking the 9:00 pew tomorrow, or did Elena need you earlier?
Same pew. I told Elena I would come after and bring soup for her freezer.
I saved you the thin book with the prayers in English and the other side.
Thank you. I like having the old words beside the new ones.
For distribution, can you handle the sign-in table instead of carrying boxes to cars?
Yes, that helps. I did my three repeats before leaving and packed the cushioned inserts.
Perfect. I will ask Luis to take the heavier carts.
Good. The concrete by the parish hall is harder on me than the kitchen tile.
Did your lights flicker too? Irving got a hard blast around supper.
They blinked twice. I waited until the rain eased, then carried over the extra battery lantern.
For Mrs. Coleman?
Yes. Her porch rail was slick, so I stayed by the steps until she got the latch open.
For Saturday, I have two folding chairs and the Spanish flyers. Can you bring the black pens?
Yes. I put pens, tape, and the blank new-address sheets in my church tote already.
Also Father Miguel said the forum questions are printed in the office if anyone asks.
Good. I want one copy too, especially the council race page.
Tomorrow's food boxes are set. Please close the binder and rest your hands tonight.
I will. I made tea and put the cream yarn on the chair before I start chasing the clues on the paper.
Good. Let the old guitar song be the last thing on, not that paper.
Fair. One side of the scarf first, then music, then lights out.
Forecast says 49 at 6 tomorrow. Linda is still in if you are.
I'm in. Same 6:15 start works, but I need to stop at 6:45 sharp.
That's fine. We'll keep to the familiar loop and skip the extra block.
Can I ask you something after the lunch rush? That vendor talked over me again but waited when Rick repeated the same answer.
Come by the office at 2:30. Bring the call notes so we can keep it factual.
You still want me on the supplier follow-up?
Yes. I also want to hear your read on it. I have been keeping a list of patterns like this before I vote on the city contract items.
Same time after dinner? I have the pharmacy paper in my purse.
Yes. I will put the kettle on and call you when the kitchen is wiped down.
I can bring the soup Saturday. Should I make enough for the freezer?
I sent you that long note from our cousin because I knew you would know what to do with it.
Did that envelope system survive the month?
Saturday still looks better than Sunday for me next week.
A few containers would help. The little kitchen freezer has space now.
You sounded wound up when you left me that voicemail. Was it the restaurant again?
It did. I left the grocery and medicine amounts alone and only sent the regular Toyota amount.
I read the first lines and stopped. No date, no clinic name, and it was trying to sell drops at the end.
Then Saturday. Just us, no extra stops.
Inventory, two call-outs, and a vendor mistake. I made cinnamon tea and rewrote the closing list twice.
You were thinking about adding extra, right?
So wait until my appointment?
Okay. I will not stay late; I know you like the house quiet after dark.
Ask your doctor, and I can also ask Mr. Chen at Walgreens when I pick up my refill tomorrow.
Did you ever call the number Janice gave you?
Not until the annual report finishes posting. The old school line still shows nothing, but I want the paper copy before I change April.
No. The card is still by the bread box. I looked at it Sunday, then started knitting the baby blanket instead.
That is fine. Also remind me to move $1,150 out before the first so the portal does not fuss.
I found the Polk Street grocery receipts from when Mama was sick. They were tucked behind your campus packet.
Keep the receipts for now. The packet can stay closed.
You were always the one checking labels, sodium, and what could stretch through Friday.
Those classes were useful right away, even if I used them at home first.
The bookstore has that Central America memoir you mentioned, the one with the chapter about mixed roots and church festivals.
Hold it for me if you can. Those stories make more sense to me than the neat little boxes on forms.
Coffee after study on Wednesday? Bishop Arts, quiet table if they have one.
Yes. I can bring the old photo of Mama's family too; the one everyone argues about because nobody fits one column.
Still want coffee after study, or is tomorrow's long shift too much?
Coffee is fine if we sit close by. I need to get home early for the towel-roll routine.
Bishop Arts, the quiet place with the short walk from the lot?
That one. I am wearing the sturdy black pair, not the flats.
The truck moved earlier. Can you come at 7:50 instead of 8:30?
Yes. I will skip my slow breakfast and bring the small cooler for the cheese.
Thank you. Mama asked if you can set aside the masa for the ladies from San Pedro like last time.
I remember them. I will label it before the line starts.
A customer is refusing to leave and Luis wants me to make the call now.
Ask Luis to step back. Offer the man water and a seat by the window while you clear the register line.
If he keeps shouting?
Then call, but write down what happened first and keep everyone using his name. Afterward we review what led to it.
Coffee after the bookstore? The Oak Cliff place has that quiet back room.
Yes, the back room is best. I left the sidewalk tables last time because the air was too much.
I also saw they have Irish coffee on the menu now.
Plain coffee for me today. I already had my little glass with Elena on Sunday.
Still on for coffee after study next Wednesday, or did the family lunch move?
Coffee still works. Saturday is the quiet meal at my place, so I am picking up squash, eggplant, and tomatoes in the morning.
I remember that pan from last time. You tucked a portion aside before anyone sat down.
Elena likes having one for Sunday. I will open just a small pour with dinner and keep the rest corked.
For the food boxes, could you spare any rosemary sprigs today, or are you keeping them for your own pot?
I can cut some after the dough rests. Tomatoes need tying first, then I can wrap the sprigs in a damp towel.
No rush. I know your mornings fill up fast when you have the oven going.
I will bring them by noon. Tuesday clothes and Thursday floors are done, so today is only counters, oven, and the back bed.
Rain stopped. Still meeting by the west entrance at 6:15?
Yes. I packed a small towel. Mama never let us leave wet footprints anywhere with polished floors.
Good thinking. That loose handrail by the steps is still bothering me.
I noticed it too. Daddy would have had a wrench on it before breakfast.
Can you watch the vendor callback at 2:00? I need ten minutes for a San Antonio call.
Yes, I can take it. Is that the Roberto call you said usually stays quick?
Yes. Just checking if his two are using the Dallas tickets or if I should pass them to Elena.
Got it. I'll leave the callback notes on your desk.
Did I catch you in the middle of your papers again?
You did, but I can talk. I just put March at 3,480 with the medicine pickup and the family lunch.
That sounds close but not wild. I will keep Saturday simple, no big grocery list.
Thank you. The 4,100 deposit gives room, but I like seeing it on paper before the week starts.
Did you ever fix that retirement line on the website?
Yes. I set it back so they add the extra part each check. Same amount hits every two weeks, so it was easy to compare.
Good. You sounded tired yesterday.
It was just the long Monday. When the door opens at 8 and I leave around 5:30, I feel every minute by supper.
I saved your serving spoons from the hall kitchen. They were in the tub with the ribbon scraps.
Thank you. I was looking for them after packing the warmers. Did the last tray of pastelitos go?
Every piece. Marisol said the older men asked who made the beans.
That means I need to start soaking earlier next time. The market was nearly out of the small red ones.
Radar looks messy again. I am waiting until 7.
Same here. If the alley drains okay, I will do my short pass by Mrs. Coleman's mailbox first.
Text me before you step out. Those puddles hide the curb.
I will. Phone charged, rain jacket by the door.
Coffee after study still good for next Wednesday? I found that used copy we talked about.
Yes. I blocked the evening before the work calendar filled it. Tasha is covering the vendor list that day.
I’m glad you kept the evening. Bring the book you borrowed if you finished it.
Finished it Sunday. I’m practicing letting the place run for a few hours without me staring at every line.
You left your bookmark in my copy again.
Keep it until next Wednesday. I still have your notes tucked in the Dust Bowl book.
Deal. And April coffee can be the first Saturday unless your schedule changes.
First Saturday works. I will bring the tote this time.
For Saturday distribution, do you want the youth group on table setup or car loading first?
Car loading first, but pair each teen with an adult. I do not want boxes stacked near the hot trays.
I will mark that. You always catch the part that saves us later.
I learned to draw the map before people arrive. Tasha is doing that at work now too.
I can cover the vendor call tomorrow morning if you need to get to the clinic desk early.
Thank you. I only need ten minutes to drop off the updated cuff sheet and the lab copy.
No problem. Want me to move the pastry tasting later too?
Please. I am trying to be careful this week, and I still have to take the night tablet before I sleep.
Coffee after study next week? You sounded worn out when you mentioned the new supervisor.
I set aside that quiet table for coffee tomorrow. Bring the book if you still want me to read the note tucked inside.
Coffee sounds good. I spent today fixing the order sheet, walking Tasha through the cooler log, and smoothing over that lunch complaint.
I will. It was in the drawer with Papi's 2011 program and Mami's 2018 card.
Do you want help sorting the rest, or just company while you decide what stays?
That is a lot for one Thursday. Did the anniversary card from the crew help at least?
Company. The binders with medicine times and night notes are harder to open than I expected.
It did. Fourteen little notes tucked in the envelope made me laugh, especially the one about the broken freezer my first spring there.
I saw your nieces' Easter photos. Sweet girls. Did you catch the parish note about palms?
Yes, that and Marisol's baleada sale flyer were the only things I looked at tonight.
Call me after 8:30 if the bill letter is still bothering you.
I will call. I don't want that mixed in with the photos and parish notes.
For Saturday boxes, should we put the apartment complex flyers in Spanish and English? Some folks said the clinic forms confused them.
